key_insight: Symmetry-based low-rank fine-tuning enables one MatterSim 1M potential to predict lattice thermal conductivity across compounds sharing a crystal symmetry.
engineering_relevance: Faster thermal-conductivity screening could support materials selection for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications; this is not a direct solar-cell performance study.
method: Select a small set of compounds sharing a crystal symmetry.
Fine-tune MatterSim 1M using symmetry-based few-shot low-rank adaptation.
Calculate lattice thermal conductivity by solving the Boltzmann transport equation.
evidence_signal: Across half-Heuslers (space group 216), space-group-225 materials, and spinels (227), the method reduced mean absolute relative differences from reference calculations by 2–3× versus untuned MatterSim 1M and cut fine-tuning time by approximately 5–7× for 100 compounds versus per-compound tuning.
watch_item: Transfer was demonstrated within shared-symmetry groups against computational references, not established for arbitrary crystal symmetries or experimental measurements.
paper_title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
